narrative.overview:
The site reads like a campaign poster for a real network. Big condensed caps, a field of logo blue and the faces and words of actual members carry the message. Every brand band (header, home hero, inner page heads, the closing call to action) is one continuous slab of the logo's EU blue, and the header merges into it so the top of each page reads as a single printed sheet. Paper sections between the bands are calm and cool white, set in Sofia Sans at reading size, so the poster moments have room to hit.

The hand-made layer comes from the brand's own materials. Hand-painted watercolor splashes in red, yellow, blue and green sit behind section headings like a marker stroke on a printed flyer. The three white bars from the top of the logo open each blue band. Member quote cards and event photos are the proof; stock imagery stays secondary. Motion is short and physical: cards lift by 2px, photos zoom 3 to 4 percent, and the quote deck fans and shuffles.

The world was set against one specific look: a darkened stock-photo hero with centred typewriter text above three identical image cards. Nothing in this system should drift back toward it.
keyCharacteristics: Logo blue fields for header, hero, page heads and the call-to-action band; deep blue for the footer.
Sofia Sans Extra Condensed at weight 900, in caps, for every display line; Sofia Sans for everything you read.
Marker yellow is the action colour on blue and in dark mode; logo blue is the action colour on paper.
Watercolor strokes behind headings, chosen only from splashes whose paint clears the image edge.
The three logo stripes as the structural mark.
Navy-tinted shadows and 14px corners on photos and cards.

rules.name: The Two Primaries Rule
rules.body: On paper, the primary action is logo blue with white text. On blue fields and anywhere in dark mode, the primary action is marker yellow with navy ink. A yellow fill on paper white has no edge (1.46:1), so it never appears there. `--primary` swaps to `--marker` in `.dark`; on blue bands in light mode use the `marker` button variant explicitly.

rules.name: The Blue Field Rule
rules.body: Logo blue is a field, not an accent. It fills whole bands edge to edge (header, hero, page head, call-to-action band) and the header has no border or shadow that separates it from the band below. On paper, blue appears only as type, links, buttons and the date block's month strip.

rules.name: The Highlight Rule
rules.body: Marker yellow on paper is a line, never a fill or text colour: link underlines (2 to 3px, offset 6px), the nav indicator and selection. As text, yellow appears only on blue or navy grounds.

rules.name: The Series Colour Rule
rules.body: Event series carry a fixed colour from `lib/event-series.ts`: Beer and Roses is red, conferences and congresses are blue, trips ("goes to", "visits") are green, everything else is yellow. The colour shows as an 8 to 10px dot before location and date on gallery tiles, gallery chips and gallery section heads. New series surfaces use `seriesColor()` and `seriesDot`, never a hand-picked hue.

rules.name: The Poster Caps Rule
rules.body: Every heading that announces a section is the `.display` class: Sofia Sans Extra Condensed, weight 900, uppercase, line-height 0.9, letter-spacing -0.005em, `text-wrap: balance`. Paragraphs, meta lines and form text are never set in the condensed face.

rules.name: The Long Word Rule
rules.body: Display headings must survive German, Hungarian and Greek. Use fluid clamp sizes, let `text-wrap: balance` work, and add `hyphens: auto` on the largest sizes, as the hero does. Never fix a heading's width to its English length.

rules.name: The Stripes Rule
rules.body: The three bars from the top of the logo (three 3px bars, 5px apart, current colour) are the structural mark. They open every blue band above the heading at 56 to 64px wide and white at 70 percent, close the mobile menu, mark the empty event image and sign off the footer at small size. Use the `Stripes` component; it replaces decorative dividers and labels.

rules.name: The Ink Shadow Rule
rules.body: Shadows are tinted with navy ink, never neutral black or grey, and they belong to physical objects. Bands, sections and nav never cast shadows.

rules.name: The Clean Edge Rule
rules.body: A watercolor stroke behind a heading uses only splashes whose paint stays clear of the image edge: blau 1, 7, 8; rot 1, 5, 6; gelb 1, 6, 8; grün 4, 5, 6, 7. Any other variant shows a straight cut line. Large field bleeds on blue bands (hero blau 4, call-to-action gelb 6) may use other variants because the band's `overflow: hidden` crops the cut edge off-canvas.

rules.name: The Paper Yellow Rule
rules.body: Watercolor strokes blend with `multiply` at 60 percent on paper and `screen` at 25 percent in dark mode. Yellow strokes are hidden in dark mode, because yellow screened onto navy turns olive.

dos: Do use marker yellow with navy ink for the main action on any blue field or in dark mode, and logo blue with white for the main action on paper.
Do pair a marker button with an inverse (white outline) button when a blue band offers two actions.
Do set every section heading with the `.display` class, at a fluid clamp size, and test it in German, Hungarian and Greek.
Do open each blue band with the `Stripes` mark above its heading.
Do pick heading watercolor strokes only from blau 1/7/8, rot 1/5/6, gelb 1/6/8 and grün 4-7.
Do colour-code event series through `seriesColor()` and `seriesDot` from `lib/event-series.ts`.
Do tint shadows with navy ink (`--brand-ink`) and add a hairline white ring to cards in dark mode.
Do use the shared easing `--ease-out-expo` (cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)) for lifts, zooms, the nav bar and the quote deck, and keep every animation off under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
Do use Ring Blue for focus indicators on paper surfaces, as inputs already do.
donts: Don't fill a button or a surface with marker yellow on paper white.
Don't set marker yellow text on paper; yellow text belongs on blue or navy only.
Don't show a yellow watercolor stroke in dark mode.
Don't set paragraphs, meta lines or form text in Sofia Sans Extra Condensed.
Don't build a darkened stock-photo hero with centred typewriter text, or a row of three identical image cards.
Don't put small tracked-caps labels or eyebrows above headings, and don't use gradient text.
Don't add new hard-coded `hsl()` or `rgba()` colours in components; add a token to `app/globals.css` first.
